label: Plan Comparison Card
title: Plan Comparison Card
summary: Use a Plan Comparison Card to compare two or three plans feature by feature, with the plan you recommend in gold.

anatomy.description: Plan names sit in a row above a dark table. Each row of the table is one feature: its label on the left, then one cell per plan, in the same order as the names.

configuration.title: Plans, features, and cells
configuration.description: columns names the plans, left to right. Mark the one you recommend with brand: its name turns gold. rows lists the features: each row’s values fill the plan columns in the same order. A string or number shows as text, false shows a grey cross, and any Coin component, such as a Badge, shows as it is. showInfo adds an info icon after a feature’s label. children replaces the table with your own content, under the same plan names. No mode restyles the card: the modes you give it pass to the components in its cells and slot.

states.title: An info icon that explains or only hints
states.description: showInfo draws the icon as a hint: it doesn’t press, and screen readers skip it. onInfoPress makes the same icon a button named “More information about” and the feature, with a bigger tap area than it looks. Use it to open the explanation, for example in a sheet. The card and its rows have no pressed, selected, or disabled state.

sizing.title: Fills its host, nothing wraps
sizing.description: The card fills the width of its host; Figma draws it at 328 px. The feature column takes 1.8 shares of the width and each plan column one share, so at 328 px two plans leave about 67 px for each value and three plans about 48 px. Text never wraps or shortens: a name, label, or value too long for its column runs into the next one. Height follows the rows: each row is 46 px, and the plan names sit 16 px above the table.

content.title: Short names, short values
content.description: Call the user’s current plan Your plan and the others by their product names, in a word or two. Write features as nouns, such as Cashback or Bonus JioGold, not sentences. Keep values to a number or a few characters: 1.25x, ₹5,000, 1%. Use false for a feature a plan doesn’t include, not the word No, so every missing feature looks the same. With three plans, keep names under about 8 characters.

sources.title: Use the public Plan Comparison Card contract
sources.description: The guide compares the Figma component with the installed package and its Storybook stories.
blocks: Installed jfs-components is 0.1.78 (19 October build of Biscuit’s main) from the team’s private package repository. Figma’s Plan Comparison Card exposes only its Slot as a property; the plan names, rows, and cells are layers there. In the package, the plan names split their row exactly 1.8 to 1 but the table’s cells don’t, because each cell’s padding counts first, so a name sits 3 to 8 px right of its column. Text never wraps or shortens and overflows narrow columns. The table is 5 px taller than Figma’s because its row lines sit outside the 46 px cells, and Figma draws no line under its third row. The info icon from showInfo and the grey cross have no accessible name. The published Storybook still shows the older generated page, with every story on a black host (all reported).
